name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
summary: A foundational breathing drill performed supine to recruit the diaphragm, encourage 360-degree abdominal expansion, and downregulate the nervous system.

setup: Lie flat on your back on a comfortable floor or exercise mat.
Bend your knees so your feet rest flat on the floor about hip-width apart.
Place one hand on your upper chest and the other hand on your abdomen just below your rib cage.
steps: Inhale slowly and deeply through your nose, directing the air low into your abdomen so your belly rises against your bottom hand while your chest remains relatively still.
Pause gently at the top of the inhalation without straining.
Exhale slowly and completely through pursed lips or your nose, feeling your belly gently fall back toward your spine.
Repeat for the target number of breath cycles or set duration.
instructions.breathing: Maintain a smooth, relaxed rhythm with nasal inhalation and a controlled, prolonged exhalation.
cues: Keep your chest and shoulders quiet

common_faults.fault: Chest breathing with excessive shoulder elevation.
common_faults.correction: Consciously relax the neck and upper traps, ensuring only the lower hand rises on the inhale.

common_faults.fault: Forcefully pushing the belly out using spinal extension rather than breathing.
common_faults.correction: Keep the lower back relaxed in a neutral position against the floor; allow the breath itself to drive the expansion.

precautions: If you feel lightheaded or dizzy, pause and return to normal, unforced breathing.
